assumptions: Sep (callKeys message): for the 3 address words of ONE call (caller, first two arguments), each balance slot is the balance slot of no other address and no allowance slot of these keys is a balance slot. SepAll (Sep for EVERY list of 160-bit keys) and Reenter.NoCollision CODE (no other byte string has the keccak256 of CODE): GLOBAL keccak hypotheses, almost certainly false. Used ONLY by the theorems listed under global_keccak_hypotheses.theorems_with_global_hypotheses. No headline depends on them.

HoldsCode L CODE state (and GoodLink = HoldsCode and Inv): the account at L holds the LINK bytecode and the invariant is stated on its storage. Assumed at the start of every real-runner and sequence theorem; kept by every proved step. Proved for one concrete state only modulo hH (holdsCode_baseState).

Inv L state at the start (sum of balances = 10^27): assumed by every supply and sequence theorem. The constructor is not modelled, so nothing here says it holds on chain. Proved for baseState modulo hu (inv_baseState).

hH : hashOf CODE != EMPTY_CODE_HASH in holdsCode_baseState, good_baseState, inv_runL_baseState. True (the #eval test Test/Hash.lean compares the hash) but not proved in the kernel (keccak of 3,153 bytes; the same computation ran a box out of memory for WBTC).
hu : Supply.UniqBal 1 CALLER1W in inv_baseState, good_baseState, inv_runL_baseState: one keccak fact about one address, never proved.

Fork: Berlin <= fork < Glamsterdam in every theorem with a CALL, in supply_all_real_local, process_good_local, create_good_local, MsgL, CreateL (one-counter gas meter). Real-runner witnesses with a contract receiver are stated from Paris. The generated frame theorems of the functions with no CALL (paths, ok_<fn>, supply_<fn>, readable, Roles, Sanity/Zero) carry only Fork.berlin <= fork and no upper bound in their statement (the ten-token audit, fix 7): they are true as stated at every such fork, because they speak about EthLib's frame runner instantiated with the one-counter meter (Evm fork Nat), but EthLib runs transactions with that meter only below Glamsterdam, so they describe the real chain only for fork < Glamsterdam. The generator was not changed to add the bound: it would be an unused hypothesis in each of them.

Gas cap: frame or message gas <= GAS_CAP = 2^60 - 1 in supply_transferAndCall, supply_all (transferAndCall case), frameKeepsQ, supply_all_real_local (bound <= GAS_CAP), process_good_local, create_good_local, MsgL, CreateL. It replaces hN (bytes length rounded up < 2^64): ok_tac_len proves hN from gas < 2^60.
hN : tacN message < 2^64 in the forward transferAndCall theorems of Tac/Main.lean and in ok_tac_whole (discharged by the gas cap in the supply results).
hdel: the receiver is not an EIP-7702 delegated account. Only in ok_tac_whole and transferAndCall_readable. The supply and sequence results do not need it (callIn_outcome_any).
message.data.size < 2^256 (part of Sane and FrameKeepsQ; hsize' in supply_all, supply_all_real_local).

Sane L CODE msg for a top-level message (process_good_local, MsgL): if it runs at L then its code is CODE and it has a target. ASSUMED for the top message, not derived from the state and the way EthLib builds a message from a transaction.

CalleeKeeps runChild message state (supply_transferAndCall, supply_all): the LOCAL assumption on the one message the CALL sends (if it ends without error from a state that keeps the invariant, the state it leaves keeps the invariant). Proved for EthLib's real runner and every receiver by calleeKeeps_processRunner_local, which itself assumes: Berlin <= fork < Glamsterdam, bound <= 2^60 - 1, HoldsCode, and CleanFrameL (above). The older calleeKeeps_processRunner_sepAll_noCollision proves it only under the global SepAll and NoCollision (not a usable fact). For a STOP receiver the restricted form CalleeKeepsOf is proved with no keccak hypothesis (calleeKeeps_stop). One run with a receiver that really calls back is exhibited (ReWit/, reenter_closed), under Sep RE_KEYS, hH and hRE.

Other steps in Seq.Run / SeqLocal.RunL (good_other, good_runL, inv_runL): a step that is not a message or creation (fees, refunds, end of transaction, account deletions, EIP-7702 authorizations) is ASSUMED to keep the code and storage of L. Not proved from EthLib's transaction layer.

hA : Sep RE_KEYS, RE_KEYS = [CALLER1W, 0x1000, 0x2000, 1] (supply_tac_re_frame, process_tac_re, msgL_tac_re, reenter_closed; ReWit/Closed.lean): the keccak separation of slots for the four address words of the reentry witness (the word 1 is there because callKeys reads the amount of the inner transfer as a possible address key). Not proved. It also gives hu for the invariant of the start state.

hRE : hashOf RE != hashOf CODE (holdsCode_reState, reenter_closed): the keccak hash of the 45 byte receiver is not the hash of the code of LINK. True, not proved in the kernel for the same reason as hH (keccak of the 3,153 bytes of the code). hH is also a hypothesis of holdsCode_reState and reenter_closed. hashOf RE != EMPTY_CODE_HASH is proved (re_hash_ne).
not_covered: The constructor and the state at deployment: nothing proves Inv (sum of balances = 10^27) or HoldsCode for the on-chain state. The base case is baseState (Sanity/Base.lean), a model state, modulo hH and hu.
History before Berlin: LINK was deployed in 2017; all CALL and sequence theorems are for Berlin <= fork < Glamsterdam, so the invariant is not carried from deployment to Berlin.

Reentry witness (audit finding LINK-4, now covered for one run by ReWit/): only ONE receiver (RE, which calls transfer(0x2000, 1) once), amount 1, empty data, one concrete start state. Not covered: a receiver that calls another function, calls back more than once or more deeply, or a run that ends with an error. The witness rests on the named hypotheses hA : Sep RE_KEYS, hH and hRE, which are not proved.
CleanL for a transferAndCall run to any receiver with code other than RE (ReWit/ shows it for RE from Sep RE_KEYS), and any instance of CleanCreateL.
Sep (callKeys message), hu and every other keccak separation fact: never discharged for any key list, so no supply or sequence theorem has a closed, hypothesis-free instance.

A concrete MsgL step from baseState (a totalSupply() call through processMessage with every hypothesis but Sep discharged): not written. A concrete run through processMessage from another closed state does exist: reenter_closed (ReWit/Closed.lean) from reState, under hA, hH and hRE; it is the closed instance of the start invariant, of the run-local keccak condition CleanL and of the sequence theorem inv_runL for LINK (the ten-token audit, fix 5).

Transaction level: fee payment, refunds, EIP-7702 authorizations in a transaction, creation at address L. Only messages through processMessage and creations through processCreateMessage are proved; the rest is the assumed Other step. Sane of the top message is assumed, not derived.
DELEGATECALL or CALLCODE sent from a frame running at L by other code (LINK itself has none): excluded by Sane and HoldsCode, not proved impossible.
Glamsterdam and later (EIP-8037 two-counter meter): not ported, by the brief.
Runs with more than 2^60 - 1 gas, and so a bytes argument of 2^64 bytes or more.

The data bytes of the second log and the call data after the head words are exact by definition (tacLog2Data, tacCallData read memory) but are not shown equal to the padded bytes argument (audit finding LINK-6: the lemma is not written). The head words (selector, sender, value, offset, length) are proved (Tac/Bytes.lean).
tac_at_call is a plain Hoare statement at one gas value; completeness around it is in ok_tac_pre and ok_tac_post.

name() and symbol(): only 'a successful run writes no storage and adds no log' (ro_name, ro_symbol), the entry theorems and the path theorems. No output, no gas, and no witness that either function returns (audit finding LINK-5: name_runs and symbol_runs are not written; their paths are loops).

transferAndCall_readable: code size is stated as a 256-bit word equal or not equal to 0; in the callee case the storage before the callee is given for all accounts and slots, the gas sent is the raw term of SentIn (with gas - 207), and the logs after the callee are not stated.
calleeKeeps_stop proves a restricted form (CalleeKeepsOf, which also fixes msg.code); the literal CalleeKeeps is proved only through the induction (calleeKeeps_processRunner_local).
The generated supply_preserved still carries selector != 0x4000aea0; supply_all and supply_all_real_local are the versions for all 12 selectors.
For a delegated (7702) callee the model follows one delegation; the message still targets the receiver. Covered by the supply results, not by the exact-message theorems.

Transaction level (fix 2 of the ten-token audit, recipe C of audits/link/fixes.json): LINK has no Tx.lean on the shared library TokenKit.Seq; the sequence theorems are over RunL with the assumed Other step. Not part of the fixes 5 to 9.
findings_contract: totalSupply is the constant 10^27 in code; there is no storage slot for it. Balances are at mapSlot a 1, allowances at mapSlot spender (mapSlot owner 2).
The dispatcher only checks that call data is not empty; there is no ABI length check, so short call data is read as zero padded. Each function checks the call value itself.
validRecipient (to != 0 and to != the token) guards transfer, approve, transferFrom and transferAndCall. SafeMath failures end in INVALID 0xfe and burn all gas.
transferAndCall writes both balances and emits both logs (ERC-20 Transfer, then the ERC-677 Transfer with data, topic 0xe19260af...) BEFORE the CALL.

The CALL at pc 3088 asks for GAS - 710 as a 256-bit subtraction: under 710 gas left the request wraps and the 63/64 rule caps it. Value 0, selector 0xa4c0ed36 onTokenTransfer(sender, value, data), output size 0.
The CALL result IS checked: a failing receiver reverts the whole transferAndCall (witness transferAndCall_reverts). Return data is never read.
A receiver with no code gets the tokens and both logs, no call is made, and the function returns true. EXTCODESIZE is tested twice (pc 2840 and 3071); the second test cannot fail.

The bytes argument is decoded with no bounds check; CALLDATACOPY at pc 604 is the first opcode that charges for the length. Decode costs 278 gas plus memory growth plus 3 per word; each copy loop costs 68 gas per word.
The free memory pointer is never moved after the decode.

A receiver can reenter the token during the CALL. The supply invariant still holds for such a run under the run-local keccak condition CleanFrameL, HoldsCode, Berlin <= fork < Glamsterdam and gas <= 2^60 - 1 (supply_all_real_local, by induction over the real runner); one concrete run with a receiver that re-enters is evaluated on the real runner (reenter_closed, ReWit/Closed.lean: the receiver calls transfer(0x2000, 1) from inside onTokenTransfer; the call succeeds and the sum of the balances stays 10^27, under the named hypotheses hA, hH, hRE).

For the owner of the repo (audit finding LINK-9): nobody can mint or burn. The code has no owner, no mint, no burn, no pause; totalSupply() returns the constant 10^27; the only storage writes are 2 balances and 1 allowance per call.
increaseApproval and decreaseApproval have NO validRecipient check (spender 0 or the token itself is accepted), unlike transfer, approve, transferFrom and transferAndCall.
No function checks the length of the call data, so a short transfer call can succeed with arguments read as zero padded.

The supply equation is a statement about all 2^160 balance slots, so it truly depends on keccak: an allowance slot equal to a balance slot would let approve change a balance. Finding one is far out of reach (about 2^128 work), but this is why the global hypothesis SepAll is not a formality and why the headline theorems now use run-local hypotheses.

global_keccak_hypotheses.result: Fix round of the ten-token audit (finding LINK-1): WBTC's run-local form is ported. The headline theorems (supply_all_real_local, calleeKeeps_processRunner_local, process_good_local, create_good_local, good_runL, inv_runL) use only: Sep (callKeys m) for messages m that enter LINK's code during the run, and 'no code deposited during the run is another byte string with the hash of CODE'. The global SepAll and NoCollision remain only in theorems that carry the hypothesis in the name.
global_keccak_hypotheses.why_global_is_not_usable: SepAll asks Sep for every list of 160-bit keys (a statement over all 2^160 balance slots and 2^320 allowance slots into 2^256 words: almost certainly false by counting). NoCollision CODE asks that no other byte string has the keccak256 of CODE (false by counting over all byte strings). A theorem that assumes them may be vacuous: it is NOT a usable fact.
global_keccak_hypotheses.approach: LinkVerify/Link/Trace.lean (copy of WBTC's, namespace changed): trace relation Sent / Occurs that mirrors runFrame and processRunner, Clean over its events, the restricted runner `only` with runFrame_agree. AnyLocal.frameKeepsQ proves Trace.FrameKeepsQ fork GAS_CAP L CODE (Inv L) SepMsg from supply_all.
global_keccak_hypotheses.global_implies_local: cleanRunL_of_sepAll_noCollision, cleanFrameL_of_sepAll_noCollision, cleanL_of_sepAll_noCollision, cleanCreateL_of_sepAll_noCollision, Msg.toLocal, Create.toLocal, Run.toLocal: the run-local hypotheses are weaker than the global ones.
global_keccak_hypotheses.missing: A closed instance of CleanL / CleanFrameL with no keccak hypothesis for a run with a receiver that has code: ReWit/ shows CleanL and CleanFrameL for the receiver RE from Sep RE_KEYS (four words), which is not proved; see not_covered.
